problem: Sara has a box of $9$ colored pencils. In how many ways can Sara pick a set of $4$ different pencils from the box?

feedback.worked_solution:
First, note that $(\frac{15}{2})$ means the same thing as ${}_{15}{C}_{2}.$

 In general, the number of combinations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{C}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!\,r!}.
$$

Substituting $n=15$ and $r=2,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{15}{C}_{2}\text{ } & =\frac{15!}{(15-2)!2!} \\  & =\frac{15!}{13!\cdot 2!} \\  & =\frac{15\cdot 14\cdot \cancel{13!}}{\cancel{13!}\cdot 2!} \\  & =105.\end{aligned}
$$
